assumptions.summary: Air temperature/humidity are constant; waves and air-transit loss are ignored; natural convection is neglected.
Body conductivity and surface temperature are constant; motion is discretized into equal-amplitude/frequency actions.
Bubble concentration changes do not alter most physical parameters; the surface layer reduces evaporation and air exchange.

contributions.summary: Balances exchange, evaporation, body, radiation, inflow, and overflow across filling, cooling, and reheating phases.
Solves a heat-conduction PDE and fits a plane surrogate with R-squared 0.931.
Represents body motion as a moved-volume/moved-distance source.
Adds a normal-distribution comfort criterion to control.
Compares continuous-flow and threshold-switch strategies by enumeration.
Modifies air-interface losses and reruns the control recommendation.
Translates the model into a direct user-facing recommendation.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Constants and variables define temperatures, density, heat capacity, flow, body, motion, and bubble quantities.
Initial field is 39 C, inlet source is 45 C, and the PDE tool generates fields at 2.5 s and 100 s.
Nominal strategy uses 0.007 L/s, 311.1 K, and a 1800 s horizon.
Nominal optimum fixes tub dimensions, transfer rates, body area, flow, outlet temperature, and 30-minute duration.

edges.handoff: The phase-aware thermodynamic balance supplies the field PDE's source, boundary, and initial conditions.
The fitted temperature field and gradient become the reduced interface in the universal thermodynamic model.
The universal energy balance is extended with a motion-dependent convection source.
Motion-adjusted temperature fields are evaluated against the human comfort distribution.
Comfort probability, temperature deviation, and water use become the Strategy I objective and constraints.
The same comfort and energy criteria are recast for piecewise tap switching.
The selected continuous strategy is reused after bubble-interface losses are modified.

feedbacks: Sensitivity and bubble scenarios return to the same control metrics; the Explanation returns the final result to the user.

independent_extensions.summary: Fit Kgrad(t) using the full PDE trajectory and report cross-validation rather than a single-time plane fit.
Calibrate motion source Fb and the response function with measured body motion and temperature sensors.
Elicit comfort/water/stability weights and test whether strategy ranking reverses under plausible preferences.
Measure bubble-layer conductivity, thickness, concentration, and lifetime before rerunning control.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A separate nontechnical explanation may improve auditability and audience communication; award status is not causal evidence.

Restatement and approach lists mirror deliverables and methods.
Flow charts expose initialization, enumeration, embedded solves, and output.
A separate audience artifact converts technical chain to user action.

models.summary: The UTM decomposes internal-energy change into wall/air exchange, evaporation, body heat, radiation, hot-water inflow, and overflow loss, then treats filling, full-bath cooling, and reheating as separate phases.

models.section: Temperature field PDE and fitted interface
models.summary: The PDE tool solves the conduction field from a constant hot-water source and Neumann boundaries; a plane fit with reported R-squared 0.931 is then used as an approximate downstream temperature distribution.
The fitted field is substituted into wall exchange, evaporation, body, radiation, inflow, and overflow terms so the average temperature and gradient can drive later motion and control models.
Each discrete movement is encoded by moved volume times moved distance; a nonnegative response function then pulls local temperature toward the average, while the source magnitude changes over time.
The body-temperature comfort model uses a normal distribution centered near 312 K, allowing a comfort probability to be combined with temperature stability and water use.

Strategy I minimizes temperature deviation, water flow, and negative comfort simultaneously under flow, safety, energy, and time constraints; enumeration returns 0.007 L/s and 311.1 K in the reported scenario.

Strategy II alternates tap-on and tap-off phases using Tmin1, Tmin2, Tb, and a binary phase indicator; the reported optimum collapses Tmin1 and Tmin2 to the same value, interpreted as a continuous limit.

Bubble water removes or reduces evaporation and replaces direct water-air exchange with a bubble-layer transfer; reported dissipation is 45.85% of normal water and Strategy I changes to 0.004 L/s at 311.9 K.

results_trace.summary: Continuous flow 0.007 L/s at 311.1 K uses 12.6 L and improves temperature decline relative to natural cooling.
Equal thresholds collapse automatic switching to a continuous process.
Bubble strategy uses 0.004 L/s at 311.9 K and reports lower dissipation.
Water consumption is more sensitive than water temperature to geometry, human, and transfer parameters.
A small continuous trickle is recommended, personalized by bath and body parameters.

section_map.summary: Name the practical problem before technical detail.
Open with a familiar discomfort, then make the modeling route answer it.
Convert everyday context into explicit deliverables and decision criteria.
Set the global scope before equations and attach a reason to each simplification.
Give a symbol ledger before equations so later formulas can be read as a connected system.
Expose the dependency graph before derivation; baseline, extensions, and final decision are visible.
Move from aggregate heat to spatial field, then explain why a fitted approximation is needed downstream.
State an executable search procedure and show the two strategy flow charts before reporting numbers.
Report parameters, curves, table values, resource use, and comfort in a layered evidence order.
Classify uncertainty by environment, water, human, approximation, and algorithm before numerical sensitivity.
Pair broad positive scope with explicit limits on parameter identification and computation.
Return from equations to the exact requested metrics and report the decision in one compact chain.
Translate technical causes into a nontechnical explanation and direct advice without repeating equations.
Close provenance without adding new reusable argument moves.

limitations: All 51 pages were rendered and visually reviewed through six contact sheets; pages 7-18, 24-33, 36-45, and Appendix code pages were inspected at full resolution.
OCR damages mathematical glyphs and units, so rendered equations and tables are authoritative.
The source lacks calibrated motion response, complete PDE/grid settings, objective-weight elicitation, empirical bath validation, and propagated uncertainty.

deliverables: Model filling, natural cooling, and hot-water addition in space and time.
Represent human motion and body comfort.
Choose a control strategy balancing temperature stability, comfort, and water use.
Compare normal and bubble bath water.
Provide a one-page nontechnical explanation for users.
task_reconstruction.reconstruction_limit: No separate official Problem A statement was located; the paper's explicit restatement and path-derived A classification are retained.
task_reconstruction.source: Summary, Introduction restatement/approach, UTM, motion/comfort/control models, bubble bath, testing, conclusions, and Explanation

title: Keep It Warm
unresolved_questions: What grid, time step, solver tolerance, and full MATLAB state reproduce the PDE surfaces and strategy results?
How should Kgrad(t) and Fb be measured or estimated from real motion and temperature fields?
How are the objective weights and comfort distribution selected for different users?
Can the equal-threshold Strategy II result be resolved by a converged hybrid or event-driven solver?
How do radiation, humidity, waves, evaporation, and bubble lifetime change the recommendation?
Can the continuous trickle recommendation be validated in a sensor-equipped bath?

verification.summary: R-squared 0.931 supports the reported approximate analytic interface.
Curves, Table 3, water ratio, temperature improvement, and comfort rate are reported together.
The degenerate continuous limit is discussed against finite-difference and objective-weight limitations.
Enumeration step sizes are translated into half-step parameter uncertainty.
The final user artifact preserves the mechanism and recommendation link.

weaknesses.summary: The fit is reported at one early time and Kgrad(t) remains unknown.
Fb is a scenario parameter requiring experiment.
Weights and standardized criteria are selected rather than empirically elicited.
Equal thresholds and finite-difference resolution make the switch strategy collapse to a continuous limit.
Several environmental and human effects are signed qualitatively without uncertainty propagation.
Step size and computing capacity limit accuracy.
More accurate field fitting, algorithms, geometry, and data collection remain open.

Open with a familiar discomfort, then make the modeling route answer it. | Begin with {familiar problem}; then state that {models} will determine {decision}.
Convert everyday context into explicit deliverables and decision criteria. | The task is to model {state} under {processes}, while keeping {quality} and limiting {resource}.
Set the global scope before equations and attach a reason to each simplification. | Assume {environment/geometry/physics}; this removes {hard mechanism} because {bounded reason}.
Give a symbol ledger before equations so later formulas can be read as a connected system. | Define {symbol} as {quantity} with {unit} before using it in {model}.
Expose the dependency graph before derivation; baseline, extensions, and final decision are visible. | Build {baseline}; hand it to {extension}; combine both in {decision layer}.

Move from aggregate heat to spatial field, then explain why a fitted approximation is needed downstream. | After deriving {energy state}, solve {field PDE}; replace it with {fitted representation} for {downstream use}.

State an executable search procedure and show the two strategy flow charts before reporting numbers. | Initialize {variables}; enumerate {candidate controls}; solve {embedded equations}; retain {best objective}.

Report parameters, curves, table values, resource use, and comfort in a layered evidence order. | For {strategy}, report {control}; compare {baseline}; quantify {resource ratio}, {quality change}, and {comfort}.

Classify uncertainty by environment, water, human, approximation, and algorithm before numerical sensitivity. | List {error family}; state whether it makes the model {warmer/cooler/uncertain}; preserve its direction as a warning.
Pair broad positive scope with explicit limits on parameter identification and computation. | Retain {capability}; bound it by {missing measurement, parameter, or computation}.

Return from equations to the exact requested metrics and report the decision in one compact chain. | The selected {strategy} yields {control}, {resource}, {quality}, and {comfort} under {assumptions}.
